maria: Heads-up — after rolling calib-v2 for INT8 we're seeing prefill slowdowns on long-context tests. Started the longctx perf suite this morning.
sam: How bad is "bad"? numbers?
maria: Quick summary from run-2026-03-18:
```
prefill fp32 baseline: 110 ms/seq
prefill int8-calib-v1: 115 ms/seq
prefill int8-calib-v2: 185 ms/seq   # +68% on long context (8k)
decode fp32/int8: ~18 ms/step (no significant change)
KV cache miss-rate: +2% (weird)
```
sam: Oof. decode unaffected but prefill jumps — suggests kernel path or batching decision change.
kevin: Could be kernel fallback to slower GEMM path for prefill (different shapes) after calibration changed activation ranges. Any kernel logs? @jin can you check kernel selection traces?
jin: Ran the profiler. I see extra kernels: `int8_matmul_block_reorder` followed by `matmul_fallback_fp32` on prefill for long seqs. Snippet:
```
[MM] selecting kernel: int8_matmul_block_reorder (fast path) -> returned ERROR_RANGE
[MM] selecting kernel: matmul_fallback_fp32 (safe path)
```
jin: Also noticed reorder kernels are memory-bandwidth heavy for >4k tokens which explains wallclock increase.
ashley: Sounds like calibration widened dynamic range, triggering different quant params -> some ops choose blocked kernels that hit slow reorder. This disproportionately affects prefill because TTFT does large single prefill batches vs decode which is small per-step.
maria: That matches queuing metrics — prefill TTFT latency escalates, but TPS (throughput) for decode stayed fine. So TTFT vs TPS tradeoff is visible here.
sam: Can we force kernel selection to the legacy int8_fast_matmul for a canary? If that regresses quality we know it's calibration/quant noise related.
deploy-bot: perf-run started: id=rw-perf-1769001, tests=[longctx-prefill-int8, longctx-decode-int8, calibration-sanity]
maria: Forced int8_fast_matmul on canary results:
```
prefill int8 (forced): 125 ms/seq (closer to baseline)
logprobs delta vs fp32: mean abs diff 0.003 -> within tolerance
```
maria: Quality delta small but still seeing rare token flips at very long prefixes (~8k). Might be quant noise at extreme context lengths.
kevin: Hypothesis: calibration-v2 reduces saturation so dynamic range improves, but quantization scale per-layer changes making some kernels pick blocked layout. Also KV cache access pattern might miss due to small numeric drifts changing cache keys? check serialization hash/details.
jin: I instrumented kvcache keys — no structural changes, but tiny float differences in projected keys lead to 0.4% more misses on some layers when using int8-calib-v2. Those misses cause extra recomputation and trigger fallback paths on some requests.
ashley: Action items:
- revert calib-v2 for default release (maria)
- add kernel-preference flag for long-context prefill (kevin)
- update batching heuristic: prefer grouping long-prefill requests differently to avoid reorder-heavy kernels (ashley)
- add regression perf test that runs longctx prefill against calib variants (jin)
- monitor KV cache miss delta as a quality/regression metric (sam)
maria: I'll open RW-987 with those tasks and link perf run logs. Assigning owners in PR.
kevin: Thanks. Also add a quick canary that forces slower path to see cost impact; good to measure unit economics.
maria: will do. :thumbsup
